title: The neighbor
hook: Jibril kept urging kindness to the neighbor until the Prophet ﷺ thought neighbors would inherit (Bukhari)
tomorrow: Removing a stone from the road

segments.voice: Yesterday: sadaqah jariyah, the well, the tree and the knowledge that keep running. Your line was the well keeps giving. Today, where charity starts. Day one hundred fifty-four.

Quick question: what's the name of the person who lives closest to you? Not your closest friend. The closest person: the other side of your wall, across the hall, next door. A lot of people don't know. They know strangers across the world by their usernames, and nod at the person ten feet away without ever learning a name. They send money to causes overseas, which is good, and have never knocked on the door beside theirs. In Islam, charity has a starting point, and it's on the other side of your wall.
screen: `WHO LIVES CLOSEST TO YOU?` → `A NOD, TEN FEET AWAY.` → `CHARITY HAS A STARTING POINT.`

segments.voice: Bukhari and Muslim report the Prophet ﷺ saying: Jibril kept urging me to be good to the neighbor, so much that I thought he would make the neighbor an heir. An heir: someone with a legal share in what you leave behind, like family. That's how often the angel came back to it. The Qur'an names neighbors in Surah an-Nisa, in a list of those to be good to: parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is related to you and the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side. And Bukhari reports a warning so strong the Prophet said it three times: by Allah, he does not believe. Who? The one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm. The hadith get practical. Sahih Muslim reports him telling the companion Abu Dharr: when you make a stew, add extra water, and look to your neighbors. Stretch the pot. Bukhari reports him telling women not to think any gift to a neighbor too small, even a sheep's hoof. And a neighbor isn't defined by faith. Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud report that the companion Abdullah ibn Amr had a sheep slaughtered, and when he came home the first thing he asked was: have you given some to our Jewish neighbor? He had heard the Prophet's words about Jibril and the neighbor. Scholars have argued over how far a neighborhood stretches. The principle is simpler than any measuring. Before the world, the house next door. Before the cause, the name.
screen: `JIBRIL KEPT URGING.` · `BY ALLAH, HE DOES NOT BELIEVE.` · `ADD WATER TO THE STEW.` · `HAVE YOU GIVEN TO OUR JEWISH NEIGHBOR?` · then, large: `START NEXT DOOR.`

segments.voice: Picture the doors nearest yours, one by one, and notice which neighbors you know and which you don't. Pick one, and picture something small you could bring: extra from dinner, a few pieces of fruit, a note with your name and number, even just a hello, since no gift is too small, not even a sheep's hoof. Picture knocking, and their face, and if it makes you nervous, breathe through it.
The neighbor. The one next door, whose rights Jibril urged so often the Prophet thought they would inherit. Today's word.
Your line: start next door. Jibril kept coming back to the neighbor. That's day one hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims give special weight to neighbors, of any faith: sharing food, visiting, helping and avoiding any harm to them, following the hadith of Jibril and the neighbor.
